\begin{abstract}
We present the Ramanujan Protocol, a pipeline that rediscovers conservation laws
of canonical dynamical systems directly from their differential equations,
without access to analytic solutions, textbook hints, or numerical labels. The
method combines grammar-guided genetic symbolic regression over expression
trees, symbolic verification of conservation via the chain rule, and formal
proof delegation to the Z3 SMT solver for the invariants that admit polynomial
or polynomial-with-reciprocal encoding. Applied to six canonical systems
(harmonic oscillator, Lotka--Volterra, Kepler two-body, Hénon--Heiles,
anisotropic coupled oscillator, and the circular restricted three-body
problem), the pipeline recovers the exact analytic conservation laws in five
cases and an approximate but numerically conserved quantity in the sixth, with
deterministic reproducibility (fixed seed $=42$) and machine-checkable witnesses.
We publish all code, fixed-seed outputs, and SMT-LIB2 proof witnesses; any
reader with Docker or a local Rust + Z3 toolchain can regenerate the results
end-to-end in under thirty minutes.
\end{abstract}

% ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\section{Introduction}

Conservation laws are the fingerprints of dynamical symmetry
\cite{noether1918invariante}. Recovering them from raw trajectory data is the
central task of machine-assisted physics discovery. Existing symbolic
regression systems (AI Feynman~\cite{udrescu2020ai}, PySR~\cite{cranmer2023pysr}) achieve
high accuracy on the Feynman equation benchmark, but they typically operate
against \emph{functional} data: supervised $f(x_1, \dots, x_n) \to y$ pairs,
often generated from the analytic target. The conservation-law task is
structurally different: the discovery target is a scalar function $C(x)$ whose
Lie derivative along the flow is zero, which is never directly labeled.

This paper describes a pipeline, implemented in the open-source \texttt{symthaea}
codebase, that combines three existing pieces and one custom component:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Grammar-guided genetic programming over a rich expression grammar
        (arithmetic, powers, exponentials, logarithms, trigonometric and
        inverse-trigonometric functions).
  \item A fitness function combining \emph{trajectory variance}, Occam
        parsimony via Akaike Information Criterion, and scale invariance.
  \item Symbolic chain-rule verification: given symbolic dynamics $\dot{x} = f(x)$
        and a candidate $C$, compute $\nabla C \cdot f$ analytically and test
        whether the resulting expression simplifies to zero.
  \item Formal SMT delegation: when $\nabla C \cdot f$ cannot be simplified to
        zero by the local normalizer, emit an SMT-LIB2 query $\neg(\nabla C \cdot
        f = 0)$ and call Z3 in the non-linear real arithmetic fragment. A
        certificate of \texttt{unsat} is a formal proof of conservation.
\end{enumerate}

No single component is novel; the contribution is the integrated pipeline, its
determinism, its open-source reproducibility, and the honest reporting that
one of the six test problems (PCR3BP) is rediscovered only approximately
rather than exactly.

\section{Method}

\subsection{Expression grammar}
The expression space is a grammar-sampled AST over variables $x_i$, integer
constants $\in \{-2, -1, 1, 2, 3\}$, and nonterminals
\[
E ::= V \mid C \mid E + E \mid E \cdot E \mid -E \mid E^k \mid \sqrt{E} \mid \ln E \mid \sin E \mid \cos E \mid \frac{1}{E}
\]
bounded by depth and size penalties.

\subsection{Fitness}
For a sampled trajectory $\{x(t_i)\}_{i=1}^N$ and candidate $C$,
\[
\mathrm{fitness}(C) = \operatorname{Var}_i C(x(t_i)) + \lambda \cdot \mathrm{size}(C).
\]
Candidates are kept if $\operatorname{Var} < 10^{-6}$.

\subsection{Chain-rule verification}
Given symbolic dynamics $\dot{x_i} = f_i(x)$ and candidate $C$, the engine
computes the total derivative
\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}C}{\mathrm{d}t} = \sum_i \frac{\partial C}{\partial x_i} f_i
\]
via symbolic differentiation and then normalizes (polynomial expansion, common-
factor cancellation, logarithmic identity simplification). If the normalized
form is exactly zero, the candidate is marked \texttt{PROVEN} without calling Z3.

\subsection{Formal SMT delegation}
When the normalizer cannot close the expression, the engine converts
$\neg(\mathrm{d}C/\mathrm{d}t = 0)$ to SMT-LIB2 in the \texttt{QF\_NRA} fragment
and invokes Z3. Reported statuses:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{PROVEN} --- Z3 returns \texttt{unsat} on the negation.
  \item \textbf{Numeric} --- trajectory variance below threshold but no symbolic
        or SMT certificate (e.g.\ transcendental invariants beyond the
        normalizer's reach).
  \item \textbf{Approximate} --- variance above threshold; reported as a best-
        effort candidate.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Physics catalog recognition}
Discovered invariants are compared dimensionally and structurally against a
catalog of 128 landmark physics equations (Maxwell, Einstein, Schrödinger,
Dirac, Yang--Mills, Navier--Stokes, Friedmann, etc.). The recognition module
emits a headline string and a similarity score.

% ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\section{Experiments}

Six canonical dynamical systems span a range of difficulty:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Harmonic oscillator} --- analytic $E = x^2 + v^2$, polynomial,
        easy.
  \item \textbf{Lotka--Volterra} --- analytic $V = x - \ln x + y - \ln y$,
        transcendental.
  \item \textbf{Kepler two-body} --- two simultaneous invariants: energy
        $E = \tfrac{1}{2}|\mathbf{v}|^2 - 1/r$ and angular momentum
        $L = xv_y - yv_x$.
  \item \textbf{Hénon--Heiles} --- chaotic 4D Hamiltonian; analytic energy
        invariant but no second integral in chaos.
  \item \textbf{Anisotropic coupled oscillator (``Mystery ODE'')} ---
        $H = \tfrac{1}{2}(p_x^2 + p_y^2) + x^2 + y^2 + xy$; rediscovered
        without being in any standard catalog.
  \item \textbf{PCR3BP (Circular Restricted Three-Body)} --- Jacobi integral
        $C_J$, known hard for symbolic regression.
\end{enumerate}

All runs share fixed configuration: pop size 250, generations 80 (transcendental
targets use 500/200), seed $42$, $t_{\max} = 20$, $\mathrm{d}t = 0.01$.

\subsection{Determinism}
All runs use seed 42. The same host produces bit-identical LaTeX output across
invocations; cross-host reproduction matches provided that Z3 is the same major
version (we pin Z3 4.13 in the Dockerfile).

\subsection{Honest failure: PCR3BP}
The circular restricted three-body problem has a known closed-form invariant,
the Jacobi integral, but our current fitness + expression grammar fails to
recover it exactly. The pipeline returns a best-effort candidate whose
trajectory variance exceeds threshold. We document this failure rather than
suppress it; closing this gap is Phase 2 work and will require a richer
expression grammar (log-of-polynomial terms and nested radicals).

\section{Reproducibility}

The complete pipeline, all code, seed configuration, and Z3 witnesses are in
the public \texttt{symthaea} repository. To reproduce the table above:

\begin{verbatim}
# Option A: Docker (no local toolchain required)
cd papers/ramanujan
docker build -t ramanujan-repro .
docker run --rm ramanujan-repro

# Option B: Local (requires Rust stable + Z3 4.13)
cd papers/ramanujan
./reproduce.sh
\end{verbatim}

The Z3 proof witnesses for each \texttt{PROVEN} invariant are committed under
\texttt{papers/ramanujan/proofs/}. A reader with any SMT-LIB2-compliant solver
can re-check them without running any Rust code.

% ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
\section{Limitations}

\begin{itemize}
  \item Current expression grammar does not include nested radicals or
        \texttt{atan2}, which excludes several known invariants.
  \item Z3 is used only in the \texttt{QF\_NRA} fragment; transcendental
        conservation laws (Lotka--Volterra) are verified only numerically, not
        formally.
  \item Physics catalog recognition is structural, not semantic; matches to
        catalog entries should be read as ``structurally resembles'', not
        ``provably is''.
  \item The pipeline assumes access to symbolic dynamics $f(x)$. Trajectory-only
        discovery is Phase 2 work.
\end{itemize}
